set.body: Phase 1 review finding 8 of 8. R/kernel.R .tiled_contraction() still requires full dense weights and atoms in memory and is tested chiefly against the same dense matrix-product formulation. It does not yet implement the architectural claim that searchlights are rows of a sparse matrix and are compiled through streamed canonical feature blocks, one relation extraction and cross-Gram formation per feature, sparse distribution, and fixed-order reduction. Implement that lowering with explicit bounded temporaries, including slices, products, and replacement allocations, and compare it with an independent dense relation/cross-Gram oracle plus algebraic laws. Done when sparse and dense representations agree, canonical block partitions are tolerance-qualified, and memory bounds are measured rather than inferred from the output tile alone.
set.title: Replace the dense contraction scaffold with the sparse searchlight kernel
